name: Judge pass rate over the chat quality cases
purpose: Judge pass rate over the chat_quality datasets on a disposable dev world: hard deterministic pre-checks first (reply text, routing, side effects, tools called), then a model judge against the case rubric and the named pivot facts. Offline validity arm (reference_replies): each case validates and its deterministic pre-checks accept a reference reply and reject an empty one The graded arm is a small stratified sample at the cheapest tier, so one case passed in one run and failed in the next and the sample cannot rank two implementations. The rubric judge (claude -p) is not yet calibrated against Joshua's verdicts, and one recorded reason (a status check that errored in the in-process transport) may be the harness rather than the chat.
record: The pass rate, passed cases out of cases run, of each implementation on the same cases, with the recorded cost as the tie-break; each run is one row of the results file pinned to the commit and the cases hash, and the leaderboard compares rows only when the hash matches.

name: Accuracy of core ML tasks over labelled cases
purpose: How often each alternative classifies a quest or input correctly, or recommends something a person accepts, on held-out labelled cases. Read in this direction: maximise correct classifications and useful recommendations on held-out labelled cases from real Quest data; minimise cost per correct answer and the number of separate classifiers that do the same job. Only the message router alternatives and the registry-conditioned intent routing have recorded runs; which-quest classification, area-of-life classification and the three recommenders have no labelled case set, and the two which-quest rankers do the same job on separate paths.
record: Accuracy of each implementation on the same cases, with cost per correct answer as the tie-break.

name: Faithful explanations per unit of cost and time
purpose: offline cases of a turn's trace with the explanation a model wrote: maximise the share of explanations whose every step is in the trace and which omit no step that changed the answer (value), at a cost per explanation below a stated share of the turn's cost and with no time added before the reply. Reads the explanation call only; explain-qar checks the documentation, not this.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. Faithfulness is judged against the trace the runner kept, so a trace that omits a step makes a fabricated step look unsupported only when the cases hold it; whether people read the explanation is not measured.

name: Whole-path turns right on a small mixed set
purpose: a dozen labelled messages spread over the kinds of request QAR serves (a question about the person's own data, an absent fact, a note, a goal, a conditional multi-step ask, an unpinned quest named only by its content, a web question, a queued hand-off, a terminal request, a request it cannot do, a bulk delete that needs a yes): maximise the share of turns that are right end to end (route, context, plan, act, answer) by the world afterwards and the reply, at a cost in model calls and time per turn that a person accepts, with no write nobody asked for.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with model calls and seconds per turn and the pass rate by kind; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. Proposed 2026-10-29 so that the whole path has one measure; the label set is small and rewritten from existing sources.
disadvantages: A dozen cases rank no two implementations that differ by a case or two, and one run of a live model varies between runs. The world is a small placeholder account behind the real tool catalogue, not a real Quest, so a failure may be the world's gap and must be read before it is called a defect. The scripted arm shows what the code around a model does for a model that is exactly right, not how a model decides.

name: What is shown of the AI's work is true, the same for everyone, and earns its place
purpose: truthfulness (hard gate), then value, then parity, on the same turns for every arm: (1) the run's emitted events pass work_trace_check (counts not overstated, no private titles in a shared thread, every step terminal) and every number, title and word shown holds against what the calls did; (2) the share of shown elements that a rubric judge says change what the person does next or build justified confidence in the answer (nothing is shown unless it earns its place; a turn with work that shows nothing earns nothing, a turn without work that shows something earns nothing); (3) parity: the settled and expanded views are the same for the sender and the other participants, solo and group, live (with a resumed stream repeating frames) and from history.
record: Per arm on the same turns: turns passed out of turns run (a turn passes when it clears the gate, has parity, shows something when there was work and every shown element earns its place), the gate failures, the parity breaks, and the pooled share of shown elements that earn their place on the real turns; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. The highest passed count is the default, labelled significant or best guess; an exact tie keeps the incumbent. Cost and time are not part of this metric: the judge runs on the Claude Code subscription.
disadvantages: The judge is the `claude-sonnet` family alias on the Claude Code subscription (exact id not logged), rubric JUDGE_RULE in score.py, one call per turn, arm and run; real turns were captured on Haiku `claude-haiku-5-5`. It is a model reading the question, the reply and the elements, so its verdicts vary between runs and it is strict about elements the reply does not cite. Offline turns are hand-built from real shapes and carry no judged value. The screenshot stage is a human-style review, not a number. The Trail's words (live line, summary, group rows) are composed by quest-frontend workTrace.ts, the file the app renders from, and printed for the judge by scripts/run-worktrace-view.js; only the plain list's own wording lives in that script. The judge reads the whole reply (it was shown 900 characters until 2026-11-01).

name: Interim messages and asks that are true, not repeated and only where a person is needed
purpose: from a turn's record (events, ledger, decision rows), never from reply wording: every interim is followed by another attempt and a later message (more-coming truth), every turn ends with exactly one final or one ask (no dangling end), an ask exists exactly when the case is blocked on a person (precision and recall), no two consecutive messages are alike and count and spacing stay within bounds (delta and bounds); met turns must not get worse (no harm). Value, whether a message tells the reader something the previous one did not, is read by a blinded judge on another model and is a reading, never the gate.
record: Per implementation on the same labelled cases (a missing credential is blocked on a person, a tool fault is not): cases passed by kind, one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. Built: the offline tier, the real policy against the incumbent and a spam baseline, no model. Not built: the real-turn tiers (one, ten, thirty on haiku through the claude CLI with the switch on) and the blinded value reading; their thresholds are unset until the first real turns exist.
disadvantages: The offline cases are labelled by construction from the design page, so they check the policy against the design and not against what people find useful; real unmet turns and the value reading are not built; the thresholds for the final tier are unset.

disadvantages: Checks structure and wording, not whether a person finds the screen useful; screenshots were read by the AI only.

name: Supported first beats within the time and cost the turn allows
purpose: offline cases of a turn's events with the beat a model wrote: maximise the share of beats whose every claim is backed by an event of the turn (value), under a first-beat time that does not delay the answer (time) and a cost per beat below the cost of the answer it precedes (cost); a beat that is refused, empty or unsupported counts against it, and a turn with narration off costs nothing. Reads the narration call only; which events exist is show-progress.
record: Per implementation on the same cases, with cost per use and time per use; one row per run pinned to the commit and the cases hash. NOT BUILT: unmeasured until its arm exists.
disadvantages: Not built: no case set, arm or command exists yet. Support is judged against the event list, not against whether the person found the beat useful; a bland beat is always supported, so a length or specificity floor is needed in the cases.
